Action Plan:
1. Provide supportive care for presumed viral upper-respiratory illness: rest, maintain adequate oral hydration, and take regular Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) for symptomatic relief.  
2. Advise patient to stay off work for the next 1–2 days to reduce infectivity and allow recuperation; reconsider return early next week depending on symptom improvement.  
3. Safety-net: if cough or systemic symptoms do not improve within 2–3 more days, or if breathlessness/fever worsens, return for clinical review; possible chest examination, vitals, and consideration of empirical antibiotics at that time.  
4. Counsel on gradual alcohol reduction: decrease to ≤2 glasses of wine per week for the next few weeks, then aim for further reduction, in view of diabetes and hypertension.  
5. Continue current long-term medications (Metformin; Lisinopril) and usual follow-up for type 2 diabetes and hypertension; no immediate change required today.  
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: Persistent, dry, continuous cough and runny nose for 5–6 days.  
• Associated symptoms: nocturnal cough disrupting sleep, chills/shivering (possible fever), generalized myalgias, lethargy. Transient diarrhea at onset (resolved). No dyspnea on exertion, chest pain, sore-throat pain on swallowing, ear pain/discharge, nausea, vomiting, urinary changes, or rash.  
• Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension. No previous surgeries reported.  
• Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented); Lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Allergies: None known.  
• Social history: Lives with partner (partner asymptomatic). Occupation—IT developer. Former smoker (quit 6 months ago). Alcohol—wine 2–3 glasses on ~3 evenings/week.  
• Family history: Father with type 2 diabetes.

Objective:
• No vital signs or physical examination findings documented in transcript.  
• No investigations performed today.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Acute cough with coryzal symptoms  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold / influenza-like illness / COVID-19) — DDx item “High”.  
   - Differential diagnosis:  
     • Acute (viral) bronchitis / post-viral cough — “Medium” (dry cough, viral prodrome).  
     • Community-acquired atypical pneumonia — “Low–Medium” (dry cough, myalgias; no focal chest signs).  
     • ACE-inhibitor–induced cough — “Low” (temporal association less likely).  
   - Investigations planned: None today; consider vitals, chest exam, ± CXR if symptoms persist/worsen.  
   - Treatment: Symptomatic care—rest, fluids, Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
   - Safety-net: Review in 2–3 days if no improvement or sooner if breathlessness/fever increases; potential empirical antibiotics then.

2. Sick-leave / infection-control advice  
   - Assessment: Need for short work absence to aid recovery and limit transmission.  
   - Plan: Stay off work 1–2 days; reassess fitness to return next week based on symptom resolution.

3. Alcohol intake in context of hypertension & diabetes  
   - Assessment: Current intake near guideline limits; reduction advisable.  
   - Plan: Cut down to ≤2 glasses of wine per week for several weeks, with goal of further reduction; reinforce during routine chronic-disease follow-up.

4. Chronic disease management: Type 2 diabetes and hypertension  
   - Assessment: Stable on Metformin and Lisinopril; no acute concerns raised today.  
   - Plan: Continue medications unchanged; maintain regular primary-care reviews and monitoring of blood pressure and HbA1c as per usual schedule.

Quality checks:
• Missing elements: No vital signs (temperature, pulse, BP, SpO₂) or chest examination documented; medication doses/routes/frequencies absent; immunisation status not discussed.  
• Internal conflict: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor conversational filler but overall good clarity.
